name: Moroccan Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemon
description: Tagine, named for the cone-lidded clay pot it's traditionally cooked in, gets real depth from preserved lemon and olives - preserved lemon's fermented, intensely savory-sour rind is genuinely different from fresh lemon, and isn't something a substitute easily replicates.
steps_detailed: Brown the chicken with the onion and garlic, 8-9 minutes.
Add the ginger, turmeric, and cumin, cooking 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add 0.75 cup water, cover, and simmer 25-30 minutes until the chicken is very tender.
Stir in the preserved lemon and olives in the last 5 minutes.

description: Couscous, tiny steamed semolina granules, is Morocco's most iconic staple, traditionally served on Fridays topped with a vegetable and meat stew.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Chickpeas (garbanzo beans, bengal gram), mature seeds, canned, drained solids

steps_detailed: Simmer the carrot, zucchini, chickpeas, cumin, and turmeric in 1 cup water 15-18 minutes until tender.
Pour the boiling liquid over the dry couscous, cover, and let steam 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Serve the vegetables and their broth over the couscous.

name: Moroccan Harira
description: Harira, a hearty tomato-lentil soup, is traditionally the first thing eaten to break the fast during Ramadan.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Chickpeas (garbanzo beans, bengal gram), mature seeds, canned, drained solids

Stir in the cilantro just before serving.

name: Moroccan Pastilla
description: Pastilla, a sweet-savory pie combining spiced meat with cinnamon-sugar-dusted phyllo, is a genuine Moroccan celebration dish, traditionally made with pigeon.
steps_detailed: Simmer the chicken with a splash of water and half the cinnamon 20-22 minutes until tender, then shred.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan until golden.
Layer the phyllo sheets, brushing each with melted butter, then add the shredded chicken and almonds.
Fold and seal, then bake at 375F (190C) for 20-25 minutes until golden.
Dust with the remaining cinnamon and sugar before serving.

name: Moroccan Zaalouk
description: Zaalouk, a smoky, garlicky cooked eggplant and tomato salad, a genuine Moroccan side dish.
steps_detailed: Roast the eggplant at 425F (220C) for 25-30 minutes until soft, then mash roughly.
Simmer the tomatoes, garlic, and cumin 8-10 minutes.
Stir the mashed eggplant into the tomato mixture and simmer 5 more minutes.
Finish with the olive oil.

name: Moroccan Harissa
description: Harissa, a fiery chili paste, is a defining North African condiment, spooned into soups and stews or spread on bread.
steps_detailed: Blend the jalapeño, garlic, cumin, and coriander with the olive oil into a smooth paste.

name: Moroccan Msemen
description: Msemen, a flaky, square-folded flatbread, a beloved Moroccan breakfast, often served with honey.
steps_detailed: Work the flour, semolina, and a little water into a soft dough.
Flatten, brush generously with melted butter, and fold into a square, laminating in several layers.
Cook in a hot, dry pan, 3-4 minutes per side, until golden and flaky.
Serve with honey.

name: Moroccan Baghrir
description: Baghrir, a spongy, thousand-hole semolina pancake, a beloved Moroccan breakfast traditionally served with honey and melted butter.
steps_detailed: Blend the semolina with water and baking powder into a thin, smooth batter.
Let rest 15-20 minutes.
Pour onto a hot, dry pan and cook on one side only, undisturbed, until bubbles rise and set into the characteristic holes.
Serve with honey and melted butter.

name: Moroccan Chicken Kebabs
description: Grilled chicken skewers marinated in real ras el hanout, Morocco's complex signature spice blend.
steps_detailed: Toss the chicken with the ras el hanout, lemon juice, olive oil, and garlic, and marinate at least 20 minutes.
Thread onto skewers and grill, turning, 8-10 minutes, until charred and cooked through.

name: Moroccan Mint Tea
description: Mint tea, sweetened green tea steeped with fresh mint, is central to Moroccan hospitality, poured from a height to create a light foam.
steps_detailed: Warm the brewed green tea with the mint 5 minutes to infuse.
Stir in the sugar until dissolved.
Pour from a height into the serving glass to build a light foam on top.

Bake at 325F (165C) for 15-18 minutes until the tops crack and the edges are just golden.
